question: Should OpenClaw permanently admit exact-ID, already-installed and enabled `workspace-directory` Codex plugins under the existing default-deny app policy?
rationale: The implementation is correct and well proven, but it deliberately revisits a recently restored curated-only product and security boundary that tests cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve narrow admission
options.body: Allow exact configured catalog IDs, require installed and enabled status, expose only owned accessible apps, and preserve zero workspace installation authority.

options.title: Retain curated-only policy
options.body: Reject workspace-directory support and preserve the current marketplace boundary established by the prior revert.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow admission
recommendation.body: Allow exact configured catalog IDs, require installed and enabled status, expose only owned accessible apps, and preserve zero workspace installation authority.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged revert that established the current curated-only behavior across these exact paths.
